scientific_facts.fact: Two sequential NADPH-dependent reductions convert curcumin→dihydrocurcumin→tetrahydrocurcumin. Both are catalyzed by the same CurA/P76113 homodimer (2subunits), not two different enzymes.

A human-fecal E. coli isolate supplied a purified82kDa enzyme of two identical subunits that catalyzed both NADPH reductions; the CurA gene was identified. The abstract does not establish that experimental isolate as K-12.

Reviewed K-12 CurA is NADPH-dependent curcumin reductase and a homodimer, with ECO0000269/PMID21467222 support. Rhea34819 and34811 describe successive conversions;34815 is their net reaction, not a third independent mechanistic step. Physiological reduction IDs are34821,34813 and net34817.
Current instructions explicitly reject single enzymes. Interpreting this two-reaction one-enzyme conversion under that boundary excludes a new record without disputing the experimental chemistry.
